newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures close lower.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures close lower.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures finished mostly lower on Thursday after spending the day in unfamiliar negative territory.

Traders said December S&Ps attempted to retrace some of the day's losses late in the session but were unable to make it back into positive territory. But dealers and locals were seen buying heavily on each dip, leading traders to believe the market will not be subdued for long.
"If anything, these people are expecting it to go higher," said one floor trader. "It does need some retracement. We're not seeing much of it but I'm glad to see something."

Jay Hohmann, head futures trader at Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette, noted that December S&Ps have moved to the top of a bull channel in recent days. As a result, there is more room for the contract to fall, while still remaining in an overall uptrend, he said.
"Generally, there's a lot of wiggle room in the market," he said. "I would not be fretful about the market even if it lost 10 or 15 S&P points."
If December S&Ps fall back towards support at 725.00, he expects the market to show signs of concern.
However, he said there is actually room for the contract to drop as low as 710.00 without falling out of the channel.
Traders saw good near-term support for December S&Ps at 743.00 even. Near-term resistance is seen between 746.70 and 747.00, they said.
Most U.S. stock index futures eased slightly early in the session after the Philadelphia Federal Reserve bank index of business conditions came out much higher than expected.
The index rose to 6.4 in November from 5.3 in October, compared with a forecast drop to 5.0, and pushed bond futures lower, dragging stocks in their wake.
Analysts said the U.S. stock market's sensitivity to bonds has only increased in a climate characterized by strings of record gains.
However, the massive profit-taking some traders predicted early Thursday never materialized. Instead, December S&Ps traded in shallowly negative territory for most of the day.

December S&P 500s closed down 0.70 point to 745.45, Midcap 400s fell 0.70 to 253.70, Value Lines rose 0.05 to 673.30, NYSE Composite eased 0.30 to 393.70 and Nikkei 225 gained 15.0 to 21,175.0. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
